Why are strings immutable in Python, and what does that mean in practice?

Supplied answer
A string object cannot be modified after creation, so s[0] = "S" raises TypeError. Every operation that
looks like a change (upper(), replace(), concatenation) returns a new string. In practice, building a big
string in a loop with += is slow; collect the parts in a list and use "".join(parts) instead.
